discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 240640
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
240 AM EDT Sat Oct 24 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dense fog will impacts portions of the area through late
  morning. An advisory is in effect.

- Otherwise, pleasant weather persists through the upcoming week
  with highs around 70, lows in the 40s, and no rain expected.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 240 AM EDT Sat Oct 24 2026

Another day with fog as the only sensible weather concern. Latest 
satellite and surface obs show dense fog rapidly expanding across 
our eastern CWA thanks to another night of light easterly flow off 
Lake Erie and prime radiational cooling. High clouds that were in 
place earlier thanks to upstream trough have now largely dissipated 
for most of the area and see no reason why fog won't continue to 
expand and persist through the late morning as suggested by plethora 
of latest guidance. Only question is how far west and south it will 
build. With light E to even ESE flow, confidence is not high for our 
southwest zones. Latest satellite shows a rapid expansion to the NW 
but very little southward expansion. Issued a dense fog advisory but 
left off the far west and southern counties for now. Will continue 
to monitor obs and expand as necessary. Surface winds finally veer 
to the south tonight and more high clouds should limit fog potential 
(save perhaps for our extreme NE areas where Lake Erie could still 
be a factor).

Highs today a near carbon copy from yesterday given no thermal 
advection. Highs do creep up a few degrees Sun and Mon as very light 
southerly flow/minor WAA takes shape. A weak backdoor front then 
brings a brief return to cool easterly flow for Tue but WAA 
increases again for Wed and Thu as a decaying cold front approaches 
the region. This front looks to stall and wash out just to our NW 
with just some very low chances for light rain near Lake MI Thu into 
Fri. Better rain chances arrive over the weekend but there is still 
a high degree of spread regarding exact timing and amounts.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SUNDAY/...
Issued at 130 AM EDT Sat Oct 24 2026

A stagnant weather pattern is allowing for a repeat fog
potential setup through early this morning. Satellite imagery 
and sfc observations indicate an expanding area of stratus and 
dense fog across northwest Ohio, with a westward movement of 15 
to 20 mph. This fog has been favored in a pattern with good 
radiational cooling and a weak easterly flow regime from the 
eastern Great Lakes. Based on satellite and observational 
trends, confidence continues to increase in dense fog potential 
at KFWA from roughly 0730Z to possibly mid morning. The greatest
uncertainty deals with westward extent of dense fog with some 
higher res guidance suggesting pockets of dense fog as far west 
as KSBN. Given uncertainty, did limit mention to MVFR vsbys 
trend by 10Z at KSBN with TEMPO IFR vsbys. Improvement this 
morning will likely be slow at KFWA given very poor mixing 
continuing. Otherwise, quiet aviation weather today as an upper 
ridge axis finally begins to shift eastward a bit, allowing for 
eventual veering of low level flow to the south late this 
period. The combination of this southerly flow and increased 
high clouds tonight should limit coverage of the significant fog
for Saturday night/early Sunday.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...Dense Fog Advisory until 10 AM EDT this morning for INZ005>009-
     017-018-024>027-116-216.
OH...Dense Fog Advisory until 10 AM EDT this morning for OHZ001-002-
     004-005-015-016-024-025.
MI...Dense Fog Advisory until 10 AM EDT this morning for MIZ079>081.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...AGD
AVIATION...Marsili

spc.summary: Severe wind/hail and a tornado are possible across portions of New Mexico and far west Texas today.
spc.text:
SPC AC 240559

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1259 AM CDT Sat Oct 24 2026

   Valid 241200Z - 251200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS OF
   NEW MEXICO AND WEST TEXAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe wind/hail and a tornado are possible across portions of New
   Mexico and far west Texas today.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper trough over the western US and Rockies is forecast to
   become increasingly fragmented as the primary vort max lifts
   northeastward from the northern Rockies into southern Canada.
   Southern portions of the main trough will be reinforced by an
   upper-level cyclone emerging from northern Baja, forecast to deepen
   modestly as it moves over the Desert Southwest. Relatively strong
   southwesterly flow aloft will precede the southern stream low
   extending eastward across New Mexico and west/southwest Texas. At
   the surface, a cold front will move southward across the Plains
   trailing from a deepening surface low in southern Canada. A much
   weaker surface cyclone is forecast to develop over the Four Corners.
   A relatively moist air mass will be enhanced by weak height falls,
   and the developing surface cyclones, which should gradually
   strengthen south-southeast winds in the lowest 1-2km AGL.

   ...Southwest and Four Corners...
   Initial ascent from the approaching upper low will begin to
   overspread the Four Corners relatively early in the forecast period.
   Despite cooler surface temperatures, the moist air mass and
   steepening mid-level lapse rates will contribute to sufficient
   buoyancy (MUCAPE 500-1000 J/kg) for storm
   development/intensification as early as 12-13z. As wind fields aloft
   strengthen (40-50 kt EBWD), at least an isolated risk for hail may
   materialize.

   More robust storm development is expected to gradually occur east of
   a weak surface trough later in the diurnal cycle as destabilization
   increases across south-central NM into northern Mexico and Far West
   TX. MLCAPE of 1500-2500 J/kg amidst modestly veering, but elongated
   hodographs promoting organized clusters and supercells. Large hail
   (1-2 inches) will be possible given the degree of buoyancy and
   cooler mid-level temperatures. The most likely corridor for larger
   hail may be confined to the greater instability reservoir across
   southern portions of the risk area. While low-level shear will
   remain on the weaker side, at least some curvature in the lowest 1-2
   km of model hodographs could support an isolated tornado risk with
   the more strongly rotating storms.

   Eventually, the meridional nature of the upper-level flow and
   increasing storm coverage should favor a transition to more
   cluster/linear storm modes into the evening across southern NM and
   West TX. Severe gusts will be possible, though eventually convection
   should weaken as it encounters a more stable and drier environment
   farther east.

   ...Northeast NM and southeast CO...
   The surface cold front is forecast to move southward over the Plains
   through the day. Ahead of it, low-level upslope flow will maintain
   modest surface moisture sufficient for weak destabilization.
   Scattered thunderstorms are expected along the frontal zone and
   across the higher terrain through the afternoon. While weak buoyancy
   should temper overall intensity, veering wind profiles could support
   occasional intensification of some clusters. A low-end risk for
   severe gusts or isolated hail is possible.

   ..Lyons/Thornton.. 10/24/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 240519

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1219 AM CDT Sat Oct 24 2026

   Valid 251200Z - 261200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   SOUTHERN AND EASTERN NEW MEXICO AND SOUTHWEST TEXAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms, posing mainly a risk for
   hail, are possible on Sunday across southern/eastern New Mexico and
   far west Texas.

   ...Southern/Eastern NM into Southwest TX...

   The upper cyclone and attendant trough over UT/AZ early Sunday will
   weaken as it lifts northeast toward the central Plains through early
   Monday. As this occurs, a belt of enhanced southwesterly mid/upper
   flow will persist across portions of the southern Rockies and
   adjacent High Plains. At the surface, a stalled surface boundary is
   forecast from central NM northeastward into the central Plains.
   Southeasterly low-level flow on the warm side of the boundary will
   maintain 50s F dewpoints across the region. 

   Cloudiness and possibly ongoing showers/thunderstorms early in the
   period lend to uncertainty regarding degree of daytime heating and
   thus, destabilization. Nevertheless, modest instability is expected
   amid vertically veering/supercell wind profiles. Elongated
   hodographs and cool temperatures near -10 to -12 C at 500 mb suggest
   isolated hail will be possible with strongest storms.

   ..Leitman.. 10/24/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 240656

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0156 AM CDT Sat Oct 24 2026

   Valid 261200Z - 271200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorm potential is expected to be low on Monday.

   ...Synopsis...

   An upper shortwave trough over the central Plains will continue
   weakening as it lifts northeast to the Upper MS Valley on Monday.
   Meanwhile, a weak upper shortwave impulse will move across the
   southern High Plains vicinity and a stronger/deepening upper
   cyclone/trough will dig over the Intermountain West. At the surface,
   a cold front will develop southward across the central Plains and
   Mid-MO Valley. Southerly low-level flow will maintain modest
   boundary layer moisture across the southern High Plains into the
   KS/NE ahead of the surface front. Instability is expected to remain
   weak, and vertical shear will also be weaker than the previous few
   days. As a result, severe thunderstorm potential appears limited.

   ..Leitman.. 10/24/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
